The appellant company was carrying on business as a dealer under the Andhra Bharat Sales Tax Act , 1948 . The respondent company was engaged in the business as well as the appellant company . The Sales Tax Officer held that the appellant was not liable to pay tax under section 10 ( 2 ) of the Act . The Appellate Assistant Commissioner held that sales of the appellant ' s business was not taxable . The High Court held that it was not open to the appellant to contend that the sales were not taxable under section 2 ( 2 )( a ) of that Act . In appeal to this Court , H EL D : The High Courts have held that in the circumstances of the case the sales of goods were not liable for the tax under the Act and that the tax was not chargeable to tax under that section . [ 8 35 B ] The High court was in error in holding that the assessee was not entitled to the tax . The question whether the sales in question were taxable under the Indian Act is a question of fact . The decision of the Tribunal is correct . [ 9 35 B C ]

The appellant was charged with the murder of one R . I . and was convicted under section 302 read with section 34 of the Indian Penal Code . The appellant contended that the conviction was bad because he was not charged with having committed the murder and that the trial court had no jurisdiction to try the case . The question was whether the appellant was entitled to the benefit of section 304 of the Code of Criminal Procedure . Held , that the High Courts have no jurisdiction in the matter of the case and the High court has no jurisdiction under section 300 of the Criminal Procedure Code . It is not necessary to decide whether the evidence of the eye witness is sufficient to sustain the conviction . The evidence of a eye witness in the case is not sufficient to justify the conviction of the accused . The circumstances of the present case are such that the evidence on the record was sufficient to connect the appellant with the crime . The fact that the appellant had been charged with an offence under section 307 of the I . P . C . is not a sufficient ground for convicting him . The mere fact that he was charged under section 326 of the IPC is not enough to justify his conviction

The assessee firm was carrying on business in the manufacture of cloth and yarn . The assessee firm carried on the business of manufacturing and selling cloth and cloth . The Income tax Officer held that the assessee was not liable to pay tax under section 10 ( 2 ) of the Income Tax Act , 1922 . The Appellate Assistant Commissioner held that it was not a business of the firm and that the business was carried on by the firm . The High Court held that there was no business of selling cloth . In appeal to this Court , H EL D : The High Courts have held that a business in a business is carried on in the course of business and the business is not carried on . The question whether the business carried on is a business carried by the assessee in the business . The decision of the Tribunal is correct . The Tribunal was in error in holding that the firm was not carrying on the trade of the company . The view taken by the Tribunal was that the income of the appellant was not carried forward . The fact that the company was carrying the business as a business was not that of the partnership . The business was carrying in the trade and the assessee could not be said to be a business . [ 8 35 B C ]

In appeal to this Court , H EL D : The High Courts below have held that a lease is a lease for a term of three years and that it is a lessee . It is not necessary to consider whether the lease has been granted by the lessee to the lessee and the lessee is entitled to acquire any land for a certain period . The question whether the lessee has been a lessee or a lessee is a question of fact and whether the lessor is a tenant or not is a matter of fact . The decision of the High Court is correct .
